records.title: 1546年：《Sharaja起义民间故事》遭禁
records.description: 理念中的Kavita诗文署注称《Folk Stories of the Sharaja Insurrection》1546被魔军查禁。只记作品禁令线索，不重建已存在的1541—1552叛乱事件。 此为已封存MOD理念的有年叙述，证据等级保持单一游戏文本；不自动修改政权、疆界或宗属。

dateEvidence.precision: explicit year in MOD narrative / diegetic quotation
dateEvidence.quote:
‘Ere the departure of summer, a
beast did find their village.
Lo! and behold – not a man, but a
boar, both tusk’d and brutish.
Skull just as thick as its hide was rose-
red, it fell upon them.
“Dvirishad, render unto me all
that you treasure dearly!”
Thus did it bleat; and so, thus did they
naught at all. It raged: “Then
burn for your insolence, fools one and
all!” – and so, it burn’d them.
All, save for Khivi, their leader; it
ask’d her why they scorn’d it.
Plainly she spoke: “The impossible,
torches cannot force of us.”
Thrown was the boar, and it bleated: “But
I did ask beforehand.”
Spoke she again: “The impossible,
torches cannot force of us.”
Anger’d, the boar did thus burn her; it
left, yet won, it hadn’t.’
– Kavita from “Folk Stories of the Sharaja Insurrection,” banned by the Command in 1546
